raw_case_text:
67-year-old female with no comorbidities; ECOG PS score = 1. Diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the right upper lobe of the lung in June 2024, stage cT4N3M0 (III-C). Pre-treatment evaluations: ECG and cardiac biomarkers were within normal ranges.
The patient completed two cycles of chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy on June 21 and July 12, 2024. Chemotherapy regimen: Pemetrexed 740 mg (Day 1) + Carboplatin 380 mg (Day 1), every 3 weeks; Immunotherapy: Tislelizumab 200 mg (Day 1), every 3 weeks.
Four weeks after anti-tumor treatment, the patient developed fatigue, bilateral ptosis, and blurred vision. Follow-up on August 1 showed elevated cardiac biomarkers: cTnT 0.195 ng/mL, CK 3,989 U/L, CK-MB 119 U/L, ALT 116 U/L, AST 208 U/L; NT-proBNP was normal. ECG showed ST-segment depression; Enhanced MRI revealed slightly uneven signals in the extraocular muscles; Coronary CTA and cardiac CMR showed no significant abnormalities.
Based on the presence of ptosis, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and abnormal ECG findings following immunotherapy, a diagnosis of possible ICIM with concomitant myositis was established.
Consequently, immunotherapy was discontinued and methylprednisolone therapy (1 mg/kg/day) was initiated. One week later, serum cTnT levels continued to rise (see Figure 4). Methylprednisolone pulse therapy (500 mg/day for 3 days) combined with IVIG (2 g/kg) was administered, but cTnT remained elevated, confirming steroid-resistant ICIM. Subsequently, tofacitinib (11 mg/day) was added, followed by mycophenolate mofetil (0.75 g BID).
The addition of tofacitinib and mycophenolate mofetil significantly improved symptoms such as ptosis, with cTnT gradually decreasing. After 3 months of anti-ICIM treatment, the patient developed chest tightness and dyspnea. Chest CT revealed newly developed multiple pulmonary inflammatory lesions, and the patient was confirmed to have PCP by etiological examination. Mycophenolate mofetil and tofacitinib were discontinued, and anti-PCP treatment was initiated. Pulmonary inflammation gradually subsided, but myocardial markers elevated again. After pneumonia control, mycophenolate mofetil was resumed at 0.5 g BID, resulting in a gradual decrease in myocardial markers. After discontinuing anti-tumor therapy for 4 months, follow-up chest CT showed stable disease (SD). Since then, the patient and her family refused anti-tumor treatment, and tumor progression occurred 5 months later.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 67-year-old female with stage IIIC lung adenocarcinoma developed fatigue, bilateral ptosis, and blurred vision 4 weeks after chemoimmunotherapy (pemetrexed, carboplatin, and tislelizumab), and subsequently presented with chest tightness and dyspnea after 3 months of intensive immunosuppressive therapy for steroid-resistant immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed in June 2024 with right upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma (cT4N3M0, stage IIIC, ECOG PS 1) with normal baseline ECG and cardiac biomarkers, the patient received two cycles of pemetrexed (740 mg d1), carboplatin (380 mg d1), and tislelizumab (200 mg d1) on June 21 and July 12, 2024. Four weeks later (August 1, 2024), she developed fatigue, bilateral ptosis, and blurred vision, and was diagnosed with immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICIM) and concomitant ocular/skeletal myositis. When initial methylprednisolone (1 mg/kg/day), pulse methylprednisolone (500 mg/day for 3 days), and IVIG (2 g/kg) failed to halt rising cTnT levels, tofacitinib (11 mg/day) and mycophenolate mofetil (0.75 g BID) were added, resolving her ptosis and lowering cTnT. However, after 3 months of combined immunosuppressive therapy for ICIM, she developed acute chest tightness and dyspnea.
subjective.past_medical_history: Right upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma, stage cT4N3M0 (IIIC), diagnosed in June 2024; immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICIM) and myositis diagnosed in August 2024; no prior baseline comorbidities.
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial ICIM onset positive for fatigue, bilateral ptosis, and blurred vision; 3-month follow-up positive for chest tightness and dyspnea.

objective.physical_examination: Baseline ECOG performance status 1; bilateral ptosis at August 1, 2024 presentation.
objective.routine_investigations: August 1, 2024 ICIM evaluation: Elevated cardiac troponin T (cTnT 0.195 ng/mL), creatine kinase (CK 3,989 U/L), CK-MB (119 U/L), ALT (116 U/L), and AST (208 U/L), with normal NT-proBNP; ECG showed ST-segment depression.
objective.advanced_workup: August 2024 imaging: Orbital contrast-enhanced MRI showed slightly heterogeneous signals in the extraocular muscles; coronary CTA and cardiac MRI (CMR) showed no significant structural or coronary abnormalities. Three months post-ICIM therapy (upon onset of chest tightness and dyspnea): Chest CT revealed newly developed multiple bilateral pulmonary inflammatory lesions, and etiological microbiological examination confirmed Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Opportunistic Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP; confirmed by etiological examination and new multifocal pulmonary inflammatory lesions on chest CT) complicating triple immunosuppressive therapy (corticosteroids, tofacitinib 11 mg/day, and mycophenolate mofetil 0.75 g BID) for steroid-resistant tislelizumab-induced myocarditis (ICIM) and myositis in a patient with stage IIIC lung adenocarcinoma. Plan and clinical course: Upon PCP diagnosis, tofacitinib and mycophenolate mofetil were discontinued and targeted anti-PCP therapy was initiated, leading to gradual resolution of pulmonary inflammation. When cardiac biomarkers rebounded during immunosuppression withdrawal, mycophenolate mofetil was safely resumed at a reduced dose (0.5 g BID) after pneumonia control, which re-suppressed myocardial markers. The patient declined further antineoplastic therapy and experienced tumor progression 5 months later.
